messages.author: 30b37db3d992e3df
messages.subject: using stan_glmer
parts:
I'm trying to use stan_glmer to experiment with different specifications for
a partial pooling model, where there's a prior covariance structure on
the coefficients; but I must be doing something wrong. Can someone provide
a template for the correct use of these models?

Thanks!

Here's what I've done: load the rstanarm package and the elections88 data. Then
(actually I'm using a sample of 1000 from the data, just to speed things up).

SEED<-12345
t_prior <- student_t(df = 7)
fmla1 <- y ~ black + female + (1 | state)

# this model follows the one in demo(ARM_Ch14). As I understand it,
# we should have a uniform prior (default prior_covariance = decov())
# on the covariance matrix.
M1 <- stan_glmer(fmla1, data = elect, family = binomial(link="logit"),
                 prior = t_prior, prior_intercept = t_prior, chains=1,
                 seed = SEED, iter = 250) # this model is a bit slow to run
print(M1, digits = 4)


# now the same model with prior_covariance explicit, and very different from uniform
M2 <- stan_glmer(fmla1, data = elect, family = binomial(link="logit"),
                 prior = t_prior, prior_intercept = t_prior, chains=1,
                 seed = SEED, iter = 250, prior_covariance=decov(regularization=5))
print(M2, digits = 4)


# these next tests all report TRUE, so adding the prior_covariance seems to have
# achieved nothing.
all.equal(fixef(M1),fixef(M2))
all.equal(ranef(M1),ranef(M2))
all.equal(VarCorr(M1),VarCorr(M2))

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: using stan_glmer
parts:
I don't think this is specific to stan_glmer, but rather to the glmer function in lme4 on which stan_glmer is based. If you run the same model with glmer there is no covariance matrix estimated because there's only a varying intercept and no varying slope. So for example, if you had (1+x|state) you would have varying intercepts by state as well as varying slopes (on whatever variable x is) by state, and a covariance matrix would be estimated. In your case you can think of it as estimating 1x1 covariance matrix, that is, just the variance of the state-specific intercept shifts. In that situation only a subset of the arguments to decov() have any effect, although it's a bit hidden in the doc in the last sentence in the Covariance matrices section in help("priors", "rstanarm"): 

A one-by-one covariance matrix is just a variance and thus does not have regularization or concentration parameters, but does have shape and scale parameters for the prior standard deviation of that variable.
 
Hope that helps, 

Jonah
